title: SIG Questionnaire Walkthrough - Sierra Payments
summary: Redwood AE+SE walked Sierra Payments through the customer's SIG/CAIQ and discussed SOC 2/ISO posture, SSO/SCIM integration, RBAC controls, audit logging and retention, encryption options including KMS and BYOK, and evidence collection for the security questionnaire. Action items include sharing a security pack, annotated SIG, SOC2 report, and scheduling a follow-up technical deep dive and test environment for evidence collection.
action_items: Alex Chen - Share annotated SIG/CAIQ export and pointer to security portal - 2025-11-14
Priya Nair - Prepare short doc on KMS BYOK workflow and sample audit log extracts - 2025-11-18
Maria Torres - Send list of highest priority SIG questions for Sierra legal - 2025-11-15
Evan Park - Kick off procurement form and confirm contract team contact - 2025-11-20
Jordan Lee - Schedule technical deep dive for VPC/private deploy with Sierra infra (30-45 min) - 2025-11-21
next_steps: Redwood to upload security packet (SOC 2, ISO27001 summary, penetration test report) to shared folder
Customer to mark priority SIG questions and return by 2025-11-15
Schedule technical deep dive for VPC/BYOK evidence and access patterns
Agree on evidence transfer method (SFTP or secure share) and retention windows
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-12
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~54 minutes
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Redwood Solutions), Maria Torres (Sierra Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (CISO), Evan Park (Procurement), Nadia Singh (IT Ops)

Auto-generated summary: Walkthrough of SIG/CAIQ items, established follow-ups for evidence and technical deep dive.

00:00 Alex (Redwood AE): all right everyone thanks for joining, will do quick intros um and then we will walk through the SIG. I'm alex, i'm your account exec here at redwood.
00:06 Maria (Sierra): thanks alex, Maria here. we'll mainly be driving the questionnaire, liaising with legal and engineering.
00:10 Liam (Sierra CISO): Liam here, i'll be focused on the risk items and third party access.
00:15 Priya (Redwood SE): hi all, priya from the solutions team, i'll cover the technical bits like sso, k m s, logs, and the dedicated options.
00:22 Alex: quick agenda, we'll open the sig/ca i q, highlight common asks (soc2, iso, sso/scim, rbac, audit logs, encryption), and note what evidence we can provide right away. any additions?
00:30 Evan (Procurement): procurement will want contract and data residency stuff highlighted, plus stages for vendor onboarding.
00:35 Jordan (Redwood): quick note, we'll also flag the dedicated and private deployment options if residency or VPC is needed.
00:40 Maria: cool, let's jump in. the first page of the sig asks for org level controls and proof of soc 2, iso. can you confirm your SOC 2 status and whether you have iso 27001?
00:48 Alex: sure, we are SOC 2 Type II in-scope for security, date on the latest report is 2025-06. we also maintain an iso 27001 certificate in our control inventory, i'll share the summary. transcript might say "s o c two" or whatever, but the artifacts are in the security pack.
00:58 Liam: ok will need the actual report, and redacted details are fine, but we need to match the sig assertions to the control mappings.
01:06 Priya: absolutely, we have a control matrix that maps SIG/CAIQ items to SOC 2 controls, and a mapping for iso as well. i'll attach a csv of that mapping.
01:14 Maria: great. next the sig asks about SSO and SCIM for provisioning, can you outline support for SAML, OIDC and just-in-time provisioning?
01:22 Priya: we support SAML 2.0 SSO today, OIDC for some flows, and SCIM for user provisioning. provisioning via SCIM is available on Dedicated and Private deployments; on Hosted we support SCIM for user lifecycle for enterprise tenants.
01:35 Nadia (IT Ops): what's your SAML IdP compatibility? we use Okta and Azure AD primarily.
01:39 Priya: Okta and Azure AD are fully supported, we've seen customers use Ping as well. SCIM endpoints are v2 spec, there might be minor attribute mapping decisions.
01:47 Liam: do you support SCIM de-provisioning and automated disabled user events? that's a must.
01:52 Priya: yes, SCIM de-provisioning is supported; we also have SCIM patch support for group membership updates.
01:58 Alex: good to note, we'll include sample SAML metadata and SCIM endpoint docs in the packet.
02:05 Maria: next is RBAC, how granular are roles and can you do least-privilege by route or per-model?
02:11 Priya: we provide role-based access controls at the org and project level out of the box. you can create custom roles with granular API permissions (route-level) and model-level scopes. for private deployments you can hook into your LDAP as well.
02:24 Maria: any segregation for token access and key rotation?
02:27 Priya: yes tokens are revocable, we support managed API keys and short-lived tokens, plus rotation policies. we also have audit logs for key usage.
02:35 Liam: audit logs — retention and format? we need at least 12 months retention for some regs.
02:40 Priya: hosted default is 90 days for detailed logs, with longer retention available as an add-on. Dedicated and Private customers can configure retention to 12 months or more and export logs to your SIEM (splunk, datadog, sumo).
02:52 Jordan: quick callout, we can also stream logs via syslog or push to cloud logging buckets in your account for long term retention.
03:00 Maria: good, we will need sample log extracts that show user actions, admin role changes, key access, and model invocation traces. can you provide those?
03:09 Priya: yes, we can provide redacted log extracts, and we'll include a sample audit log schema.
03:16 Alex: note for the questionnaire: when they ask about "who has access to customer data" that maps to our roles and the data plane, we'll clarify that Redwood engineers do not have access to customer data in Dedicated/Private by default and for Hosted there's strict access controls and documented break-glass with audited approvals.
03:33 Liam: can you explain more about the break-glass and emergency access process?
03:37 Priya: we have playbooks, escalation lists, and each incident requires a documented justification, approval by on-call manager, and the event is logged to our incident tracker and audit logs. we'll provide sanitized incident examples as part of the pen test/incident summary.
03:50 Maria: encryption at rest and in transit, and bring your own key (BYOK) — what's the support story?
03:56 Priya: all customer data in transit uses TLS 1.2+. at rest we use encryption via cloud provider KMS. for Private and Dedicated we support customer-managed keys (BYOK) and HSM integrations; for Hosted we support customer KMS integration via cloud KMS IAM policies — and we can do envelope encryption patterns.
04:14 Liam: if we do BYOK, we need clear documentation showing key rotation and how logs show KMS operations. can you produce that?
04:20 Priya: yes, we'll include a KMS operations doc and sample audit entries showing encrypt/decrypt API calls.
04:26 Evan: for procurement, any special compliance add-ons that change pricing or contract terms — for ex long retention or dedicated logs export?
04:33 Alex: yes those are typically add-ons in the contract. we'll surface pricing and include details in the proposal.
04:39 Maria: data residency — we are processed in eu only, some data can't leave region. do you offer region pinning?
04:44 Jordan: we do region pinning; Hosted customers can be restricted to a region we operate in (we have eu-west and us-west regions), Dedicated gives you a dedicated pool in a chosen region, and Private gives full control. for strict residency we recommend Private or Dedicated with clear egress policies.
04:59 Nadia: if we choose Dedicated or Private, what is the onboarding timeline and access model?
05:04 Jordan: Dedicated is typically 4-6 weeks for capacity and networking, Private (VPC/on-prem) depends on infra but usually 6-12 weeks; we'll include a runbook.
05:13 Maria: SIG section on vendor incident response — do you have SLAs or timelines for notifying customers?
05:18 Priya: we have an incident notification policy in our SOC2 and we commit to notify customers within 72 hours for incidents that materially impact confidentiality or integrity; for critical vulnerabilities we do immediate notifications. documentation will be in the packet.
05:28 Liam: curious about penetration tests and external assessment frequency.
05:31 Alex: we do annual external pentests and quarterly internal scans. we will share the executive summary and remediation timeline.
05:38 Maria: the SIG asks for encryption key custody and whether keys are stored in your environment. can you be explicit?
05:44 Priya: by default keys are in our managed cloud KMS; if you require BYOK we can rotate and you retain primary control. we do not retain plaintext customer secrets; envelope keys are used.
05:55 Maria: are there restrictions on exporting evidence or certain logs with pii?
06:00 Priya: we can provide redacted logs, and for pii we recommend you mark the sensitive fields and we'll coordinate a secure transfer method.
06:08 Evan: timeline for delivering initial evidence set?
06:10 Alex: we can upload the security pack and annotated SIG within 48 hours, SOC2 redacted within 72 hours, and then follow-up technical artifacts within a week.
06:18 Maria: perfect. one of the sig questions is about change management and software release controls, can you give an overview?
06:24 Priya: we have an sdlc with code review, ci/cd gates, automated tests, and pre-flight canary rollouts. we keep release logs and deployment approvals; we'll share a release process flow diagram.
06:35 Liam: access reviews and privileged access management?
06:38 Priya: quarterly access reviews, RBAC enforcement, and privileged accounts are on a separate approval workflow. all admin events are logged.
06:45 Maria: ok next — do you do customer-specific penetration testing or vulnerability assessments on demand?
06:50 Alex: for enterprise customers we can coordinate targeted assessments and provide temporary test environments; there is usually a legal MOU and scope set.
06:58 Maria: for the SIG there's often a request for sample evidence for data flow diagrams and network segmentation. can you provide network diagrams?
07:05 Jordan: yes, network diagrams, segmentation charts and our data flow diagrams will be included. for private deployments those diagrams will reflect customer network.
07:13 Nadia: about PKI and certificate rotation — how often are certs rotated?
07:16 Priya: cert rotation follows industry practices, service certs on standard cadences, and we monitor expiry. we'll include our certificate management policy.
07:24 Liam: any third party subprocessors list?
07:26 Alex: yes we'll share a current subprocessor list; it's in the security portal.
07:30 Maria: last chunk — operational security questions: do you have vulnerability disclosure and a public vulnerability program?
07:37 Priya: yes, security@redwood.com (note: actual contact) and we have a vulnerability disclosure policy. we also have a bug bounty program run through a vendor; we'll include the program scope.
07:47 Evan: procurement will want the high level pricing impacts for retention and private deployment so we can budget.
07:52 Alex: understood, we'll attach pricing tiers to the proposal.
07:56 Maria: ok let's talk specifics on SIG line items: question A1 (access control) wants proof of least privilege, where do you want us to start marking questions red/amber/green?
08:05 Alex: if you can mark the top 20 questions you care about (risk-critical), we'll prioritize. for each red/amber we'll supply evidence or a mitigation note.
08:13 Maria: we'll do that. any recommended deliverables we should expect in the packet?
08:17 Priya: recommended: annotated SIG with links, SOC2 redacted PDF, ISO summary, pen test exec summary, audit log schema sample, KMS BYOK workflow doc, SAML metadata, SCIM attributes example, network diagrams, subprocessors list.
08:33 Maria: perfect. next, for evidence transfer we have a requirement to avoid public buckets unless they are encrypted and access limited. how do you prefer to share?
08:41 Alex: we can use a secure S3 in our account with limited presigned links, or set up a customer-owned bucket to push artifacts. we can also use a secure upload in the security portal.
08:52 Nadia: can we do direct SFTP into a customer-managed location?
08:54 Jordan: yes SFTP or direct push to your SIEM/Log bucket is doable. we'll agree on method in the next week.
09:00 Maria: ok any limitations on how much log data you'll ship? if we request 12 months we might be charged?
09:06 Alex: for large exports there may be export fees or an add-on. we'll include cost estimates.
09:12 Liam: final question for now — can engineers at Redwood access customer model inputs in Hosted for debugging? what are controls there?
09:19 Priya: for Hosted, support access is tightly controlled; engineers can request session-based access for troubleshooting which requires approvals and is logged. We also have a policy to only access anonymized or redacted data unless explicit consent is given. For Dedicated/Private the default is no engineer access unless you enable it.
09:40 Maria: good. let's recap and assign actions.
09:44 Alex: recap: redwood to provide packet with annotated SIG, SOC2 PDF, iso summary, pen test summary, KMS doc, sample logs. customer to send prioritized SIG items by 11/15. schedule tech deep dive for vpc/b y o k and log exports. procurement will start contract dialogue.
09:58 Evan: sounds good. I'll follow up with contract contacts and get procurement items moving.
10:03 Alex: thanks everyone, we'll send the files to the shared secure folder and follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive.
10:09 Maria: thanks all.

End of transcript.
